title: The simplicial homotopy-category reflector is left adjoint to nerve and preserves products
statement: Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products, standard simplices and ordinary nerves from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in any fixed sufficiently large universe. For a small simplicial set $S$, let $\tau S$ be the ordinary category generated by its vertices and edges, imposing that degenerate edges are identities and that the long edge of every $2$-simplex equals the composite of its two short edges. Simplicial maps induce functors on these presentations. Write $N(D)$ for the ordinary nerve of a small ordinary category $D$. Then $\tau$ is left adjoint to $N$: there are natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(\tau S,D)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(S,N(D))$. The counit $\tau N(D)\to D$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $D$. For all small simplicial sets $S,T$, the canonical comparison $\tau(S\times T)\to\tau S\times\tau T$, induced by the two projections, is an isomorphism, naturally in $S,T$. No quasicategory assumption is imposed on $S,T$.
